To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bacterial expression of polypeptides is more environmentally friendly than SPPS and that it can be used for the preparation of longer polypeptides (e.g. for miniproteins).

bacterial expression is the best option for the preparation of (15) N/(13)C-labelled polypeptides of any length, while SPPS is a more suitable method for the preparation of shorter unlabelled polypeptides.
the choice of the method for polypeptide synthesis is dictated by the size of the peptide and its aggregation propensity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of GPCR ligands based on short polypeptide sequences.
the development of new, more efficient and environmentally friendly methods for the production of polypeptides and small proteins.
the development of new methods for the synthesis of biologically active peptides and polypeptides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bacterial expression is the best choice for long polypeptides (>30 aa. and for (15)N and/or (13)C labelling purposes.
bacterial expression systems are not only for protein production, but also for making pure polypeptides, miniproteins and even small peptides of different length and structure.
the method of choice depends on the specific case and that there is no universal method for all cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the "best" synthetic method for a specific polypeptide depends on the length and the folding propensity of the polypeptides.
for short, unlabelled polypeptides, SPPS is still the method of choice.

for short polypeptides SPPS is the method of choice for the production of (un)foldable, nonaggregating polypeptides, whereas for long polypeptides (miniproteins) the method of choice would be E.coli bacterial production, which is also applicable for the production of isotopically labelled polypeptides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the method of choice for a given polypeptide depends on its length and aggregation propensity.

the method of choice for a particular synthetic task depends on the specific properties of the polypeptides to be prepared, their length, purity, aggregation and folding properties and on the synthetic yields.

, in order to make a rational choice between these two synthetic routes, the researcher should consider the length of the target polypeptide, its aggregation propensity and the desired purity and yield of the final product.
